Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Haploid test: allele-resolved AP-1 reporters
ideas.description: Use SNP-resolved allele-specific RNA FISH or dual-color knock-in reporters at the two alleles of an AP-1 target (e.g., AXL, SERPINE1) to test whether the same allele remains the high-expressing one across days and through cell division. Allele-autonomous, cis-restricted persistence implies chromatin-encoded memory rather than a diffusible trans-factor set point.

ideas.title: Leash-and-unkennel: pulse-release kinetics of Fos/Jun
ideas.description: Place FOS/JUN under optogenetic or dTAG/auxin degron control, deliver a defined pulse, then fully remove the factor and measure the decay half-life of the downstream state (ATAC accessibility, target RNA, drug-resistant colony formation) relative to division time. Persistence across many divisions after the input is gone is the operational signature of memory; rapid relaxation marks it as a maintained steady state.

ideas.title: Instructor versus terminator: lineage-barcoded causality
ideas.description: Combine barcode lineage tracing (Rewind/FateMap-style retrospective clone recovery) with sorting on an AP-1 activity reporter to test whether AP-1-high cells are the same clones that later survive drug selection. Pair with timed gain- and loss-of-function to distinguish AP-1 as an instructive writer of the state, a permissive reader, or merely the terminator of an already-established transition.

ideas.title: Relocable marks: identifying the physical memory substrate
ideas.description: Run a CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag time course for AP-1 occupancy, H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and nucleosome positioning at primed enhancers after factor withdrawal, plus DNA-FISH/Hi-C for enhancer repositioning and mitotic-chromosome staining for AP-1 bookmarking in synchronized cells. This separates heritable chromatin marks that outlive the factor from simple re-recruitment of AP-1 each cycle.

ideas.title: Tachylalia and esperance: burst kinetics and anticipatory re-stimulation
ideas.description: Use MS2 live-cell imaging of an AP-1 target to quantify whether the remembered state is encoded in burst frequency versus amplitude, and measure sister-cell correlation of burst frequency after mitosis. Then compare a second stimulus pulse to a naive first pulse: faster and larger reinduction, plus inherited burst frequency, is a quantitative memory signature distinguishable from residual mRNA or protein carryover.
